ratings.comment: Worked on group essays all semester, he made the draft due date before Thanksgiving, then sent feedback 10 days later saying he was short on time. After only getting 4 comments, he messed up our scheduled office hour meeting and didn't offer to reschedule so we never got feedback. Basically made it impossible to make changes for the final version.

I never felt like the professor actually cared about us learning the material. Extremely hard cumulative exams with random specifics from lectures instead of overall concepts and definitions, as well as a horrible study guide and more, just made it feel like he wanted us to struggle and wouldn't do anything to see that we actually learned.

Albert Einstein would fail this course bc of the professor. 2 cumulative exams worth 60% of grade, randomly scheduled quizzes, a group project w/ 2 months to write a draft and then he says he's "short on time" to grade them after leaving himself 10 days to grade 20 paper drafts, and extremely niche questions from lecture slides. Save your money.

I'm a senior and have never felt the need to comment on a professor until now. As an environmental science major who has taken calc, bio, chem, etc. this is by far the most miserable elective class to take because of the professor. Extremely niche and difficult exam questions, unfair grading, bad organization, etc. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS.

Unfair course. The content on exams and quizzes was based on little statistics never emphasized during lecture. I had a tech issue during the midterm which significantly impacted my grade - never was addressed and I reached out many times with zero response. I only missed a few lectures and at this point will feel lucky if I scrape by with a B.

This guy completely abandoned the previous professor's platform that gave past students As and Bs in this class (Avg. GPA from 2006-2024 was 3.6). The exam and quiz questions are overly niche and specific, so it makes studying extremely difficult.

I believe that he doesnt want students to fully succeed grade wise like the previous professor

This class was absolutely diabolical. The lectures were lengthy and were tested on very obscure statistics rather than overall concepts. The tests and quizzes (which were 60% of the grade) felt more like a trivia game show that nobody knows the answers to, rather than an assessment that actually went through course concepts.
Do not waste your tuition money on this class.

where do I even start? The quizzes and exams in this class were by-far the most atrocious abominations of assessments that I have taken in my 7 semesters at UW. No backtracking to previous questions + honor lock. Be prepared to memorize every little detail of the slides and readings, as most questions are just random statistics and facts from them.

Overall Professor Limaye's lectures were super interesting and well delivered, and we had a lot of cool guest speakers in the class. However, the tests were definitely way harder on the multiple choice section than I ever expected based on the prepared study materials, so be prepared to remember basically everything from the slides.
Could be a good guy if he didn't want his students to fail.

Wow,don't even know where to begin. He loves to give students trick questions and each question is designed to stump you. Do not take his class. You have a higher chance passing a calculus based quantum mechanics organic chemistry biomolecular phd class taught in a different language than the one you speak. Ruined my love for this topic.

As a pre med student who has gone through the chem, physics, and bio cycle, this was the worst choice of an elective that I could've possibly made. He had the audacity to provide a pathetic attempt at a study guide that truly couldn't have helped less. I have never felt the need to leave a rate my professor review, but my experience was that bad.

It's clear he's passionate but his expectations of his students are impossibly high, and also fails to communicate them. This dude expects you to remember every little thing. The quizzes are horrible, the exams are horrible, they test you on things that are far too specific and don't actually test you on your understanding of the content.

It has been the worst class I've taken my entire undergrad as a biology major simply due to Dr. Limaye. He knows the content well but the content he emphasizes is in no way applied to the quizzes/tests (he tests on random stats and nothing emphasized in class) and is seems to have no respect for students. Overall just bad.

If I could go back in time to avoid ever taking this class, I would. They should change this class's name to ENVIRST 502: Air Pollution & Must Memorize Everything and Commit 100 Hours a Week to Maybe Get an 80%.

Prof. Limaye replaced the old prof who taught the course for the past decade. He has made the class a dumpster fire. Avoid at all costs. Grade is determined by 5 open book quizzes that are extremely difficult. 30 minutes for 15 questions with no back tracking. Exams are unreasonably difficult. Slow grading. No TAs. Do not recommend.

Prof Limaye replaces Prof Kanarek and totally changed the class. He's passionate but not experienced teaching. Syllabus was vague and not true to word. Open quizzes, group paper, midterm/final. Few points and tons of tiny details to memorize. Not an enviro major, took this class b/c it looks interesting, boy do i regret it. Pls take a diff class.

Dr. Limaye is a nice guy, but a really tough professor. The class has 5 quizzes over the course of the semester which are open-book, but really technical. YOU MUST REMEMBER EVERY. SINGLE. DETAIL. Exams are honorlock and closed book, even worse than the quizzes. Grading is very slow and inconsistent. Prepare to study a lot.

This entire class is a bait and switch. Prof Limaye takes on a very casual and fun air during lectures, and it's clear he knows his stuff, but when it comes time for the (VERY FEW) graded pieces of work, the questions are hyperspecific, convoluted, and graded harshly. 50% of your grade isn't determined until the end, and outside help is minimal.

He is knowledgeable about air pollution but makes quizzes and exams hard for no reason and doesn't care about his students. He makes quiz answers and midterm only viewable during office hours, that are hard to book. Final exam study guide is not sufficient. There is so much information in the class and it is hard to know what you should know.

Although pf Limaye has a good attitude and shows like he really care about pollution (not student) in class. But he has hard quiz and exam. quiz is open book but it tested really detail things from a bunch of reading lists and is really worky and no effective information content slides. Exam is a closed-book, but u need to remember everything.
